title.value: Revisiting Transfer Functions: Learning About a Lagged Exposure-Outcome Association in Time-Series Data
title.justification: The title of the paper clearly states the main focus, which is to revisit transfer functions in the context of lagged exposure-outcome associations in time-series data.
title.quote: Mamiya H, Schmidt AM, Moodie EEM and Buckeridge DL (2022) Revisiting Transfer Functions: Learning About a Lagged Exposure-Outcome Association in Time-Series Data. Int J Public Health 67:1604841.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the use of transfer functions to estimate time-lagged exposure-outcome associations in time-series data, focusing on environmental exposure and food marketing impacts.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper's focus on time-series analysis and transfer functions for exposure-outcome associations does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development goals.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Environmental exposures often show a time-lagged association with outcomes... We provide a case study to capture the time-lagged association between weekly purchasing outcome of sugar-sweetened drinkable yogurt and weekly-varying display promotion of these beverages.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus on statistical modeling techniques for time-series data does not align with any specific Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
primary_category.quote: To fit distributed lag models without specifying lag length, we revisit transfer functions (TFs), a method to specify time-lagged associations commonly used in econometrics and introduced to epidemiology in 1991.

primary_sub_category.justification: The exploration of transfer functions and lagged associations in time-series analysis is not directly tied to any specific sub-category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_sub_category.quote: TFs capture a time-lagged exposure-outcome association using a structural variable... We illustrate a simple form of TF to capture a commonly observed shape of lag pattern.

new_primary_category.justification: This category reflects the paper's focus on statistical methodologies in the context of epidemiological studies, specifically dealing with time-series analysis of exposure-outcome associations.
new_primary_category.quote: We revisit transfer functions (TFs), a method to specify time-lagged associations commonly used in econometrics and introduced to epidemiology in 1991.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically deals with time-series analysis using transfer functions to understand lagged exposure-outcome associations, fitting within this sub-category.
